claims.text: The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy is a single-phase fcc high-entropy alloy with coercivity below 100 Oe.
The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has suppressed orbital magnetic moments.
Magnetic moments in the fcc and hcp configurations of Fe-Co-Ni-Ti are nearly identical.
Similarity between fcc and hcp magnetic states lowers the magnetic-entropy contribution to stacking-fault energy.
Annealing at 900–1100 °C can precipitate a Ti-rich B2 or Heusler-type secondary phase in an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy.
The heat treatment will produce a dual-phase microstructure with a lamellar or dispersed secondary-phase morphology while retaining an fcc matrix.
A secondary-phase fraction of 10–30 vol% will balance magnetic pinning efficacy against continuity of the fcc matrix.
Coherent or semi-coherent fcc/secondary-phase interfaces will generate local lattice strain.
The interfaces and associated strain will disrupt uniform magnetic exchange coupling in the fcc matrix.
Local strain fields and chemical segregation around the secondary phase will alter the magnetic ground state.
The altered magnetic ground state will prevent the magnetic moments of fcc and hcp configurations from converging.
Breaking the fcc/hcp magnetic-state similarity will increase the magnetic-entropy contribution to stacking-fault energy.
The dual-phase microstructure will enhance orbital-moment alignment in the fcc matrix.
Phase boundaries will act as strong magnetic-domain-wall pinning sites.
The proposed dual-phase alloy will have coercivity exceeding 100 Oe.
The dual-phase alloy will retain a magnetic ordering temperature significantly above room temperature.
A continuous fcc matrix will preserve ductility despite the secondary phase.
The design is valid only while the fcc matrix remains continuous and the secondary phase does not cause complete fcc-to-hcp transformation or excessive brittleness.
Comparing phase-confirmed single-phase and dual-phase specimens by magnetometry can distinguish their magnetic contributions.

Failure to obtain both coercivity above 100 Oe and a magnetic ordering temperature above 300 K in the dual-phase material, or failure to increase its fcc-matrix orbital moment, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis specifies incoherent or semi-coherent interfaces, whereas the structural mediator specifies coherent or semi-coherent interfaces. Semi-coherent interfaces overlap, but the alternative interface states are inconsistent.

The conditions describe 300–600 K as significantly above room temperature, while 300 K is approximately room temperature; the falsification threshold of T_C > 300 K therefore does not establish the claimed 'significantly above room temperature' regime.
